Supplemental European Economic Area (“EEA”), United Kingdom (“UK”), and Switzerland Privacy Statement If you are resident within the European Union (“EU”), European Economic Area, Switzerland, or the United Kingdom, please read this section carefully as it will supplement the other provisions of this Privacy Statement. 1. How We Use Your Personal Data We will use your Personal Data only when the law allows us to do so. Most commonly, we will use your Personal Data in the following circumstances: Where you have given us your consent, for a specific purpose. Where we need to perform the contract, we are about to enter into or have entered into with you. Where it is necessary for our legitimate interests (or those of a third party) and your interests and fundamental rights do not override those interests. Where we need to comply with a legal or regulatory obligation. Where necessary for scientific research purposes. Where we need to protect your vital interests or the vital interests of another natural person. Where it is needed in order to perform a task in the public interest or to exercise official authority. Generally, you will have the right to withdraw your consent at any time by contacting us using the contact information listed in the “ How To Contact Us ” section above. We have set out below, in a table format, a description of all the ways we may use your Personal Data, and which of the corresponding legal bases we rely upon to do so. We have also identified what our legitimate interests are where appropriate. Note that we may process your Personal Data for more than one lawful basis depending on the specific purpose for which we are using your data. Please contact us if you need additional details about the specific legal basis we are relying on to process your Personal Data where more than one basis has been set out above in the section entitled: “JURISDICTIONAL SUPPLEMENTS: SUPPLEMENTAL NOTICE TO CALIFORNIA RESIDENTS – How we Use Your Personal Data.” 2. Change of Purpose We will only use your Personal Data for the purposes for which we collected it, unless we need to use it for another reason and that reason is compatible with the original purpose. If we need to use your Personal Data for an unrelated purpose, we will notify you and we will explain the legal basis which allows us to do so. We may process your Personal Data without your express knowledge or consent, in compliance with the above rules, where this is required or permitted by law. 3. Clinical Trials To the extent that Dyne may undertake clinical trial studies within the EEA, Switzerland or the UK, we may also use information from clinical trial participants’ medical records and other health data in order to conduct clinical or scientific research to improve healthcare. Dyne may contract with specialized service providers, such as Contract Research Organizations (“CROs”), clinical trial sites or other service partners, typically as data processors, to collect the Personal Data of the participants of the clinical trial and to manage the clinical trials that we sponsor. We may then process key-coded or pseudonymized Personal Data of clinical trial participants which means that we do not have direct or immediate access to their identifiable Personal Data (except, for example, to comply with legal requirements such as those related to our pharmacovigilance obligations). We would have a legitimate interest in using information related to your health for research studies when you agree to take part in a research study by providing your informed consent to participate. Our exception to the general provision at Article 9(1) of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), or other analogous provision, not to process special categories of data is that processing is necessary for scientific research purposes in accordance with Article 89 of the GDPR, or other analogous provision. This means that we will use your Personal Data collected in the course of a research study when we act as the data controller for such studies in the ways needed to conduct and analyze the research study. Your rights to access, change or move your Personal Data may be limited, as we need to manage your information in specific ways in order for the research to be reliable and accurate. If you withdraw from the study, we will keep the information about you that we have already obtained. To safeguard your rights, we will use only the minimum Personal Data needed for these purposes. In addition, the Personal Data of potential and actual site investigators, employees or contractors may also be collected directly by Dyne or through the CRO that we may work with and is typically used, for example, to verify the individual’s qualifications, satisfy documentation requirements for the purpose of the clinical trial, to verify financial disclosures to avoid any conflict of interest and to otherwise conduct and analyze the research study. Please see the “How We Use Your Personal Data” section of the “Jurisdictional Supplements: Supplemental Notice to California Residents” above for additional information about the collection and use of Personal Data. 4. International Transfers of Personal Data Dyne is headquartered in the United States of America, so the processing of your Personal Data may involve a transfer of data outside the EEA, Switzerland or the UK. Whenever we transfer your Personal Data out of the EEA, Switzerland or UK, we ensure an adequate and similar degree of protection is afforded to it by ensuring at least one of the following safeguards is implemented: We will only transfer your Personal Data to countries or entities that have been deemed by the applicable supervisory authority to provide an adequate level of protection for Personal Data; We will only transfer your Personal Data to countries or entities pursuant to the terms of binding data processing agreement and (as applicable) an agreement to comply with standard contractual clauses or binding corporate rules, each as approved by the European Commission or other regulators, as applicable; We will only transfer your Personal Data to countries or entities pursuant to the consent of the individual to whom the Personal Data pertains; or We will only transfer your Personal Data to countries or entities as otherwise authorized by the applicable laws and requirements of the EEA, UK or Switzerland. 5. Your Data Protection Rights This section provides information on the rights that you may have under EEA, Switzerland or UK law in relation to your Personal Data. Under certain circumstances, individuals located in the EEA, Switzerland or UK have the ability to exercise the following data protection rights: To access their Personal Data. To correct their Personal Data. To erase their Personal Data. To object to the processing of their Personal Data. To restrict the processing of their Personal Data. To transfer their Personal Data. To not be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling. To withdraw any consent that they have previously provided for the processing of their Personal Data. APPI uses distinct terms, including “personal information,” “personal data,” and “retained personal data,” so, as used herein, those terms have the meanings assigned to them under APPI. Separate privacy information may apply to particular services, programs, or relationships. Clinical-trial participants receive study-specific informed-consent and privacy materials before enrollment. Those materials provide more detailed information about the processing associated with the relevant study and should be read together with this Supplement. 1. Personal Information We May Handle The personal information we handle depends on an individual’s relationship with us and may include: Contact and professional information, such as name, business contact details, employer, title, professional qualifications, and correspondence. Investigator, study-site, contract research organizations (“CROs”), laboratory, or vendor information, such as qualifications, training, financial disclosures, contracts, and trial-administration records. Safety, medical-information, and product-quality information, including information contained in adverse-event reports, medical inquiries, product complaints, and related follow-up communications. Clinical-research information, such as coded or key-coded study data, laboratory or imaging results, efficacy and safety information, and limited identifiable information where necessary for safety, regulatory, quality, reimbursement, legal, or similar purposes. Website, device, and communications information described in our general Privacy Statement. Other information provided to us by the individual, an authorized person, or a research or business partner. Typically, we will receive only coded or key-coded study information rather than information that directly identifies a clinical-trial participant. The investigator site typically maintains the participant’s identity and source medical records, subject to the applicable protocol(s), agreements, regulation(s) and law(s). 2. Purposes of Use We may use personal information for the following purposes, as applicable: Planning, conducting, monitoring, analyzing, documenting, and supporting clinical trials and other research sponsored or supported by us. Evaluating the safety, tolerability, efficacy, quality, and performance of investigational products and supporting product development. Receiving, assessing, following up, documenting, and reporting adverse events, product-quality complaints, medical inquiries, and other safety information. Preparing regulatory submissions and communicating with the Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency (PMDA), the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW), and other competent authorities in Japan and other countries. Selecting and qualifying investigators, sites, CROs, laboratories, consultants, and vendors; administering agreements; reviewing financial disclosures; and managing study and business relationships. Conducting monitoring, audits, inspections, quality assurance, compliance reviews, investigations, and legal or regulatory recordkeeping. Analyzing research results and communicating or publishing results in aggregated or other appropriately protected form, as described in the applicable study materials and permitted by law. Responding to inquiries, operating and securing our systems, establishing or defending legal claims, and carrying out the additional purposes described in the general Privacy Statement. Using personal information for another compatible purpose or a purpose that is separately notified or consented to where required by law. 3. Special Care-Required Personal Information Some information handled in connection with clinical research, safety reporting, or medical inquiries may constitute “special care-required personal information” under APPI. This may include certain medical history, diagnoses, treatment information, health-examination results, disability information, and other health-related information that falls within APPI’s statutory definition. Genetic, biometric, image, audio, or video information may also constitute special care-required personal information depending on the information revealed and the manner in which it is processed; such information is not automatically special care-required personal information merely because of its format. Where APPI requires consent to acquire special care-required personal information, the party acquiring the information will obtain the individual’s consent or rely on an applicable statutory exception. Consent to participate in a clinical trial and any consent required under APPI to acquire or transfer personal data are separate legal matters, although they may be documented in the same study materials. 4. Clinical Trials in Japan We sponsor clinical trials in Japan and works with investigator sites, CROs, laboratories, and other research partners. We generally seek to receive coded or key-coded study information and may receive identifiable information where necessary for safety, regulatory, quality, reimbursement, legal, or similar purposes. Before enrollment, clinical-trial participants receive study-specific informed-consent and privacy materials describing the collection, use, disclosure, international transfer, retention, and protection of information for the relevant study, together with the appropriate contacts for questions and requests. Those study-specific materials provide the more detailed notice for processing associated with that study and should be read together with this Supplement. Withdrawal from a clinical trial does not necessarily require deletion of information already collected or prevent processing needed for participant safety, regulatory compliance, scientific integrity, legal obligations, or other purposes described in the study-specific materials and permitted by law. 5. Service Providers and Other Recipients We may entrust personal information processing to CROs, laboratories, safety vendors, hosting providers, professional advisers, and other service providers within specified purposes. We take measures to select and supervise entrusted parties as required by applicable law and contract. We may also provide personal data to investigator sites, healthcare professionals, regulatory authorities, affiliates, research collaborators, transaction counterparties, or other recipients with consent or another basis permitted under APPI Article 27. A recipient’s legal role depends on the particular processing activity and applicable law. The specific recipients and roles applicable to a clinical trial are described in the study-specific materials where required. 6. Transfers Outside of Japan Personal data may be transferred from Japan to our headquarters in the United States, the European Economic Area (“EEA”), the United Kingdom and Switzerland and to other recipients outside Japan, including CROs, laboratories, safety vendors, service providers, affiliates, collaborators, and regulatory authorities. The destination countries and recipients depend on the relevant activity or clinical trial. Where APPI requires consent for a transfer to a recipient in a foreign country, the party making the transfer will provide the information required by APPI before obtaining that consent. For clinical-trial participants, the applicable study-specific materials provide the operative information about relevant destinations, recipients, protective measures, and consent. Where permitted by APPI, a transfer may instead be made to a recipient that has established a system designed to provide protections equivalent to those required under APPI, or on another basis permitted by law. In such cases, the transferring party will take the measures required by APPI to support continued implementation of the relevant protections and will provide information about those measures upon request to the extent required by law. Where personal data is received in Japan from the EEA, the United Kingdom or Switzerland based on an applicable adequacy decision, the additional APPI Supplementary Rules applicable to that transfer will be followed. 7. Retention We retain personal information for as long as reasonably necessary for the purposes described in this Supplement and the general Privacy Statement and for the periods required or permitted by applicable law. We, investigator sites, our clinical-trial in-country representative, and other trial parties retain the records for which each is responsible under J-GCP and other applicable legal, regulatory, scientific, safety, contractual, and litigation requirements. 8. Security and Incident Response We maintain administrative, physical, and technical safeguards designed to protect retained personal data, taking into account the nature of the information and the risks involved. We will report qualifying security incidents to the Personal Information Protection Commission and notify affected individuals as required by APPI or other applicable law or regulation. 9. APPI Article 32 Disclosure of Information Concerning Retained Personal Data We disclose the following information regarding the entity responsible for retained personal data covered by this Supplement: Legal Entity: Dyne Therapeutics, Inc. Physical Address: 1560 Trapelo Road, Waltham, Massachusetts 02451, USA Corporate Representative: Legal Department Usage Purposes: See Section 3 of this Supplement, above, and any applicable provisions of our Privacy Statement. Security Controls: See Section 9 of this Supplement, above. Request and Complaint Procedures: See Section 11 of this Supplement, below. 10. Individual Rights and Requests Subject to APPI’s requirements and exceptions, an individual may request notice of purpose, disclosure of retained personal information and certain third-party provision records, correction, addition or deletion of inaccurate information, cessation of use or erasure where statutory grounds exist, and cessation of third-party provision where statutory grounds exist, pursuant to Articles 33, 34 and 35, respectively. A request may be limited or denied where APPI or another applicable law requires or permits. If we do not take all or part of the requested action, we will provide the notice required by law and will endeavor to explain the reason. Requests concerning retained personal data that we hold may be submitted by email to: privacy@dyne-tx.com . We may request information reasonably necessary to verify the requester’s identity and authority. An authorized agent may submit a request as permitted by law. Our response to an individual’s personal information request may be limited or denied where APPI or another applicable law requires or permits. Clinical-trial participants should ordinarily submit study-related questions and requests through the contact identified in the study-specific privacy materials. 11. Questions and Complaints Questions, requests, or complaints concerning our handling of personal information may be submitted to: Email: privacy@dyne-tx.com Regular Mail: Dyne Therapeutics, Inc., Attn: Legal, 1560 Trapelo Road, Waltham, Massachusetts 02451, USA 12. Changes to this Supplement We may update this Supplement from time to time. We will post the updated version and revise the “Last Updated” date. Where required by law, we will provide additional notice or obtain consent before materially changing how personal information is handled.

475.text: dyne therapeutics, inc. consumer health data privacy policy Submitted by admin on Fri, 16 Oct 2026 - 14:49 1. Purpose This “Consumer Health Data Privacy Policy” describes how Dyne collects, uses and/or processes Consumer Health Data in connection with this website and any of our other websites, mobile applications, online services that link to this Privacy Policy (collectively referred to as the “Sites”) or otherwise. Consumer Health Data generally means personal information that is linked or reasonably linkable to you and that identifies your past, present, or future physical or mental health status. This policy supplements Dyne’s Privacy Statement and applies to personal information defined as “Consumer Health Data” which may be subject to the Washington State My Health My Data Act (“MHMD”) or similar laws addressing the governance of Consumer Health Data. 2. Consumer Health Data We Collect We may collect your Consumer Health Data depending on the context of your interactions with us and the choices you make (including your established privacy settings), the services, products and features you use and applicable law. Consumer Health Data may include the following categories: Information about your health-related conditions, symptoms, status, diagnoses, testing, or treatments (including procedures, medications, or other interventions). For example, we may collect such information in the course of providing products or services to you or in response to your questions or requests for information. Information that could identify your attempt to seek health-related services or information. Other information that may be used to infer or derive data related to the above or other health information. 3. Sources of Consumer Health Data We may collect Consumer Health Data directly from you, from your interactions with our products, services, communications, business associations and from third parties or publicly available sources. 4.0 Why We Collect and Use Consumer Health Data We may use your Consumer Health Data for the following purposes: 4.1 To operate our Sites. We may use your Consumer Health Data to: process and manage registrations you make through our Sites; provide information about our research, services, products, offerings, disease education or related resources; communicate with you regarding our programs, events, or activities for which you may have registered, including by sending you technical notices, updates, security alerts, and support and administrative messages; understand your needs and interests, and personalize your experience with our Sites; provide support and maintenance for our Sites; and respond to your requests and questions. 4.2 To send you marketing and promotional or educational communications. We may send you communications regarding our products, services, offerings or relevant disease education or related resources as may be permitted by applicable law. You will have the ability to opt out of marketing and promotional communications. We encourage you to consult our main Privacy Statement at “ Marketing Use of Your Personal Data ”, above. 4.3 To comply with law. We may use your Consumer Health Data as necessary or appropriate to comply with applicable laws, lawful requests and legal processes, such as to respond to requests from government authorities. 4.4 With your consent. We may use or share your Consumer Health Data with your express consent, such as if, e.g., you consent to allow us post or publish your testimonials or experiences, you instruct us to take a specific action with respect to, or which may require the use of, your Consumer Health data, or you opt into third-party communications for the purposes of marketing and/or provision of products or services. 4.5 For compliance, fraud prevention and safety. We may use your Consumer Health Data as necessary or appropriate to (a) enforce the terms and conditions that govern use of our Sites; (b) protect legal rights; or (c) protect, investigate and deter against fraudulent, harmful, unauthorized, unethical or illegal activity. See the “ How to Exercise Your Rights ” section below for more details on the controls and choices you may have. 5.0 Third Parties with Which We May Share Consumer Health Data We do not share your Consumer Health Data with third parties without your consent, except in the following circumstances: 5.1 Affiliates. We may disclose your Consumer Health Data to our subsidiaries and corporate affiliates for purposes consistent with this Privacy Statement. 5.2 Service Providers. We may share your Consumer Health Data with companies and individuals that provide services on our behalf, for example, patient support services, infusion service providers, specialty pharmacies/distributors, educational offerings, provision of products or other support, hosting, analytics, communications delivery, marketing, and database management services. These parties use personal information only as directed by us and in a manner consistent with this Privacy Statement and Dyne’s privacy practices. 5.3 Compliance with Laws and Law Enforcement; Protection and Safety. We may disclose information about you to government or law enforcement officials or private parties as required by law, and disclose and use such information as we believe necessary or appropriate to (a) comply with applicable laws and lawful requests, such as to respond to requests from government authorities; (b) enforce the terms and conditions that govern use of the Sites; (c) protect the rights, privacy, safety or property of users of our Sites and (d) protect, investigate and deter against fraudulent, harmful, unauthorized, unethical or illegal activity. 5.4 Business Transfers. We may sell, transfer, or otherwise share some or all of our business or assets, including your Consumer Health Data, in connection with a business transaction (or potential business transaction) such as a merger, consolidation, acquisition, reorganization or sale of assets or in the event of bankruptcy, in which case we will make all reasonable commercial and legal efforts to require the recipient to honor the terms of this Policy and our Privacy Statement. 6. Changes to This Consumer Health Data Privacy Policy We reserve the right to amend this Privacy Policy but if we make material changes that significantly impact your privacy rights, we will notify you by updating the date of this Privacy Policy and posting it on the Sites. We may, if required by law, also provide notification of changes in a manner reasonably likely to reach you, such as via e-mail (if you have provided your contact information) or through the Sites. 7. How to Exercise Your Rights and Contact Us Some laws, including but not necessarily limited to the MHMD, provide certain rights to covered state residents with respect to Consumer Health Data, including, for example, the right to confirm, access, delete, or withdraw consent relating to such data, subject to certain exceptions. To inquire as to and, if applicable, exercise any of the rights described above, or if you have any questions or concerns about this Consumer Health Data Privacy Policy, you may contact us at any time through any of the following methods. Mail: Dyne Therapeutics, Inc., Legal Department, at 1560 Trapelo Rd, Waltham, MA 02451 Email: privacy@dyne-tx.com If your request to exercise a right is denied, you may appeal that decision by contacting our privacy support at 1560 Trapelo Rd, Waltham, MA 02451. If your appeal is unsuccessful, you may be eligible to raise a concern or lodge a complaint with the Washington State Attorney General (if you are a resident of Washington State), the Nevada State Attorney General (if you are a resident of Nevada) or another state’s attorney general office depending on your state of residence.
